lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: Consider moving Experience above Education for engineering roles.
items.because: The work may be more relevant than the degree history.

items.says: Standardize date formatting, number and measurement notation, and US or UK spelling.
items.because: The résumé uses US locations.

items.says: The skills list is short compared with the technical detail in Experience.
items.because: It omits tools and methods central to that work.

items.says: Make sure the code or portfolio link works and leads directly to relevant work.
Consider adding a LinkedIn profile.
items.because: It may support the applications.

items.says: Check that the city and country format matches the other location entries.
Specify how diagnostic accuracy was measured, the baseline, and the evaluation data or scope.
items.because: Readers need context to judge the result.

items.says: Explain “domain adapter” and “validated tool-use trajectories.”
items.because: The method may be unclear to readers outside the team.

items.says: Clarify what “in-scope signals” means.
Explain how reviewer disagreement was measured and identify the evaluation set or period, if applicable.
items.because: The 14% and 6% figures need context.

items.says: Expand GRPO on first use or explain it elsewhere.
Clarify the evaluation conditions behind “equal accuracy.”
Say how latency was measured.
Use US spelling for “penalises.”
items.because: The résumé should use spelling consistently.

items.says: Clarify what counted as an accuracy regression.
items.because: It may not be obvious to the target audience.

items.says: Consider naming the evaluation scale or set.
items.because: It would help readers assess the result.

items.says: The fine-tuning and loss-masking bullet repeats work in the first internship bullet.
items.because: It adds no separate outcome.

items.says: The backlog and signal-screening result is duplicated in the Research-Agent project section.
items.because: The résumé should keep the claim in one place or distinguish the project work.

items.says: Explain the backlog measurement period or starting point.
items.because: The 68% reduction may need context.

items.says: Clarify whether the memory figure is peak memory and identify the models or workload tested.
items.because: The 4x result needs measurement context.

items.says: Say whether model quality was maintained.
Use consistent multiplication-sign formatting.
State whether the latency figures came from load tests or production and under what workload.
Clarify how the 200 ms build threshold relates to the reported 180 ms result.
“Maintained” and “adds” have a tense mismatch.
items.because: The first verb is past tense and the second is present tense.

items.says: Explain what “release cycles to 3 days” means and give the previous cycle time.
Specify the contribution behind “Maintained.”
items.because: The verb is broad.

items.says: Clarify whether the services or their scheduled jobs were migrated.
Add a measurable impact for removing the nightly backlogs, if available.
Clarify whether “Owner” is a formal role or means the project was led.
items.because: The heading should communicate responsibility clearly.

items.says: Give concrete evidence of adoption or remove the claim.
items.because: This is the least specific project bullet.

items.says: Explain what changed and how the delivery and downstream outcomes were known to improve.
items.because: “Accelerating delivery and improving outcomes” is vague.

items.says: Clarify what the 100x growth in raw conversation is measured against.
Define what “working context” includes.
Provide evidence that useful information was preserved, if possible.
items.because: Staying within a token limit alone does not show that.

items.says: Explain what the 50-way fan-out represents.
items.because: It could refer to concurrent requests or tasks.

items.says: Explain how resolution of the deadlocks and lost results was verified.
Name the most relevant citation and faithfulness metrics, if space allows.
Clarify the personal contribution to the integration.
Add a repository link.
items.because: It would help substantiate the open-source work.

items.says: Clarify what the Kendall correlation was calculated between.
items.because: The result would be more interpretable.

items.says: Explain what the degradation levels represented.
items.because: The result would be more interpretable.

items.says: The pending-case backlog result duplicates the Mobility Systems Company bullet.
items.because: It should be removed here or clearly distinguished as a separate result.

items.says: Git is listed under Programming even though it is a version-control tool, not a programming language.
Kubernetes is listed under ML & Agents even though it is a deployment or platform tool.
